---
title: "Use"
---

No special command is needed: the host selects the skill when a task matches. Name it ("Use lucid-writer to…") to force it.

## Prompts for daily work

Tighten prose:

```text
Tighten this paragraph by ~20%. Preserve scientific meaning, numbers, citations, and caveats.
```

Draft Results:

```text
Turn Figure 3, this model table, and these notes into a concise Results subsection. Do not add literature or causal interpretation.
```

Revise a Discussion:

```text
Restructure this Discussion around the main answer. Separate observation, interpretation, alternatives, limitations, and implications.
```

Review a full manuscript:

```text
Audit the manuscript against the figures, tables, and supplement. Prioritize evidence and argument problems before prose. Do not rewrite yet.
```

Remove generic prose:

```text
Remove generic AI/LLM-sounding prose. Preserve technical terminology, claim strength, uncertainty, numbers, and citations. Do not optimize for AI detectors.
```

More examples are in [`examples/quick-start.md`](https://github.com/mdmanurung/lucid-writer/blob/main/examples/quick-start.md).

A review ends with a **Not checked** list: what the review could not see, test or chose to skip, such as figure images or sources that were not supplied.

## Always-on mode

In Claude Code, the plugin can apply its prose rules to every reply, not only to writing tasks. It is off by default.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/lucid-writer prose` | plain-prose rules for chat and commit messages. No evidence rules, so not for scientific claims. `lite` still works for one version |
| `/lucid-writer full` (or `on`) | prose plus the evidence ceiling for any finding you state, and a voice for deliverables |
| `/lucid-writer off` | turn always-on off |
| `/lucid-writer status` | show the current mode and flag path |

A change applies from the next session start or `/clear`. Saying "stop lucid-writer" turns it off for the rest of the session only. The mode lives in `~/.claude/.lucid-writer-mode` (or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). The rulesets are [`hooks/rules/prose.md`](https://github.com/mdmanurung/lucid-writer/blob/main/hooks/rules/prose.md) and [`hooks/rules/full.md`](https://github.com/mdmanurung/lucid-writer/blob/main/hooks/rules/full.md); together they add about 4,900 characters to each session.

In `full` mode the evidence ceiling applies everywhere, but the voice applies only to deliverables: manuscripts, abstracts, reports, response letters, text written into `.md`, `.tex`, `.qmd` or `.docx` files, and text pasted for revision. Chat and commit messages follow the plain-prose rules. The hook loads the first voice it finds: `.lucid-writer/voice.md` in the project, then `~/.claude/lucid-writer/voice.md`, then the plain [`hooks/rules/voice-default.md`](https://github.com/mdmanurung/lucid-writer/blob/main/hooks/rules/voice-default.md). Each is capped at 4,000 characters. The voice sets rhythm and wording only; it cannot add claims or remove hedges.

To draft a voice from your own papers, run [`voice_profile.py`](https://github.com/mdmanurung/lucid-writer/blob/main/skills/lucid-writer/scripts/voice_profile.py) with `--out ~/.claude/lucid-writer/voice.md` (or a project's `.lucid-writer/voice.md`) and `--author-position first|sole|other`. It fills only measured fields and verbatim samples, and warns when you are not first or sole author.

`full` adds at most one sentence the source lacks, a design caveat or an open question, marked `[AUTHOR CHECK]`. Markers stay inline while drafting. Ask for final, clean or submission-ready text and they move to a list after the text.

The hooks need `node` on `PATH` and do nothing when it is missing. Always-on works in Claude Code only; Codex has no session hooks, but the skill itself works there.

## Learned rules

In Claude Code, the plugin can learn your writing rules. Say "always write X" or run `/lucid-writer:learn "<rule>"` and it stores one **proposed** rule. A proposed rule does nothing until you approve it with `/lucid-writer:rules approve <id>`. `/lucid-writer:rules` also lists, rejects and retires rules.

- **What it learns:** style rules (wording, preferred and banned terms, voice) and evidence rules that only tighten, such as "always report confidence intervals". A rule that loosens a fixed non-negotiable, such as allowing "drives" for correlations or skipping citation markers, is refused.
- **Where rules live:** `~/.claude/lucid-writer/rules.json` (or under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) and, per project, `.lucid-writer/rules.json`. A project file loads only after you run `/lucid-writer:rules trust`, which records its sha256; any edit needs trust again. Until then one notice line replaces its rules.
- **What the model sees:** active rules, one line each, under `## Learned writing rules` at session and subagent start, in `prose` and `full` mode. The block is capped at 2,000 characters; extra rules show as "N rules not shown". Nothing is injected when always-on is off.
- **Nudge:** when your prompt has a correction word (always, never, don't, do not, stop, prefer, instead of, from now on) and the last reply wrote or edited a `.md`, `.tex`, `.qmd`, `.docx` or `.txt` file, the hook adds one line asking Claude to offer `/lucid-writer:learn` once. In `full` mode a prompt that names a rewrite or quotes 15 or more characters also counts. `/lucid-writer nudge off` turns it off; the flag is `~/.claude/.lucid-writer-nudge`.
- **From ratings:** `/lucid-writer:learn --from-ratings` takes text pasted from the bench page (calibration and rewrite rows with `read=` and `note=`) and proposes rules from the notes. You choose which to store.

Learning needs the hooks, so it works in Claude Code only; Codex keeps the skill without it.

## Review subagents

Three read-only reviewers ship with the skill for high-stakes work. They return findings; the main agent reconciles them and owns every edit.

| Reviewer | Checks | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence auditor | claims against analyses, figures, tables, protocols and sources | a substantial draft or claim audit |
| Skeptical reviewer | the central argument, alternatives, scope, inferential gaps, through methodological, domain, applied and statistical lenses | a Discussion, major revision or pre-submission review |
| Manuscript preflight | title, abstract, body, figures, tables and supplement for stale or contradictory content | the step just before release |

Skip them for grammar fixes and ordinary edits: they cost extra tokens and help mainly when a fresh context reduces anchoring, or when many files need review.

```text
draft or revise with lucid-writer
        ↓
evidence auditor ─────┐
                      ├─ in parallel, read-only
skeptical reviewer ──┘
        ↓
main agent reconciles and revises
        ↓
manuscript preflight
```

The installer places them in `~/.claude/agents/` (`lucid-*.md`) and `~/.codex/agents/` (`lucid_*.toml`); the Claude Code plugin loads them on its own. The skill works without them. Platform details are in [`docs/subagents.md`](https://github.com/mdmanurung/lucid-writer/blob/main/docs/subagents.md).

## Project state

For a long-running manuscript, keep a brief, a claim ledger and a decision log in the project:

```bash
python3 skills/lucid-writer/scripts/init_project.py .
```

This creates `.lucid-writer/` with `brief.md`, `claims.csv`, `outline.md`, `decisions.md` and `review.md`. The brief has a *Known weaknesses* field: limitations the authors already acknowledge, which reviewers treat as context unless the title or abstract claims more than they permit.

For stable author or team style, copy `skills/lucid-writer/assets/voice-profile.md` to `.lucid-writer/voice.md`. Voice never overrides evidence or reporting requirements.

## Mechanical checks

The helpers need Python 3.11 or newer and only the standard library. On Linux and HPC systems without `python` on `PATH`, call them with `python3`. On RHEL 8, `python3` is 3.6 and fails with `SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined`; call `python3.11` instead.

```bash
# release and style cues: placeholders, causal verbs, filler
python3 skills/lucid-writer/scripts/lint.py manuscript.md

# claim ledger: header, labels, supported claims with evidence
python3 skills/lucid-writer/scripts/validate_ledger.py .lucid-writer/claims.csv
```

The linter is not an AI detector and does not judge scientific validity.
